article_content: Scientists have created metals so hydrophobic that water droplets bounce off them. Researchers at the University of Rochester used lasers to etch microscopic patterns into metal, giving it 'super' hydrophobic properties. Unlike Teflon, a coating applied to metal, the laser-etched metals are more durable. The invention could prevent rust, stop airplanes icing up, improve sanitation in developing countries, and make efficient solar panels. Professor Chunlei Guo and Anatoliy Vorobyev used a precise laser-patterning technique to create nanoscale structures in metal. Their material is so water-repellent that it needs to be tilted less than five degrees for liquid to slide off, compared to 70 degrees for Teflon-coated materials. The technique involves extremely powerful, ultra-short laser pulses to change the metal's surface. The etchings are part of the surface and won't rub off. The material allows water droplets to collect dust, cleaning the surface and leaving it dry. It could be used for self-cleaning surfaces and more efficient water collection in developing countries. The research is supported by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.

Tofauti na Teflon, ambayo ni mipako tu, metali zilizotengenezwa kwa leza ni imara zaidi. Utafiti huu unaungwa mkono na Shirika la Bill na Melinda Gates.

article_content: A dramatic video captured the moment a bus veered off the edge of a cliff on Bolivia's infamous 'Road of Death'. The footage shows the driver navigating a treacherous section of the Bolivian pass as a crowd attempted to guide him. Despite a man's efforts to assist the driver by gesturing for him to steer away from the edge, the bus eventually tipped over. Heavy rainfall had made the 'Camino de la Muerte' road slippery and muddy, increasing the danger. The bus fell 50 metres into a ravine, resulting in the driver's death. This 38-mile stretch from La Paz to Coroico is known for its high fatality rate, with estimates suggesting 200 to 300 deaths annually. The road was dubbed the 'world's most dangerous road' by the Inter-American Development Bank in 1995. The driver had discharged all 50 passengers before attempting to navigate the perilous path alone.

article_content: It is one of the most amazing 'selfies' ever taken. The Rosetta spacecraft sent back this breathtaking image of itself as it orbited just 16km from comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko, 297 million miles (478 million km) from Earth. The image was taken on 7 October and captures the side of the Rosetta spacecraft and one of Rosetta's 14 m-long solar wings, with the comet in the background. Using the CIVA camera on Rosetta's Philae lander, the spacecraft has snapped a 'selfie' at comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko from a distance of about 16 km from the surface of the comet. The Rosetta probe will launch its Philae robot from a distance of about 6.2 miles (10km) to Comet 67P on 12 November. The 220lb (100kg) lander will reach the surface on 12 November after a seven-hour descent. It will make a gentle landing on the comet at walking pace, using screws and harpoons to secure itself on the surface.

Picha hiyo ilichukuliwa mnamo 7 Oktoba na inakamatwa upande wa chombo cha anga cha Rosetta na mrengo mmoja wa solar wa Rosetta wenye urefu wa mita 14, na nyota ya nyotama ikiwa nyuma. Chombo cha anga cha Rosetta kitatuma roboti yake ya Philae kutoka umbali wa maili 6.2 (kilomita 10) hadi kwenye nyota ya nyotama 67P tarehe 12 Novemba.

article_content: Campaigning in the French presidential election resumed on Thursday after a violent confrontation between police and Mohammed Merah, the suspect in a series of killings that shocked the nation. Merah, who was wanted for the murders of three French paratroopers and four people at a Jewish school in Toulouse, had told police he trained with al Qaeda in Pakistan. Most candidates suspended their campaigns after the latest shooting but resumed normal activities following Merah's death. President Nicolas Sarkozy visited Toulouse to offer condolences to the victims' families. Other candidates, including Francois Hollande and Marine Le Pen, also paid their respects. The crisis initially brought a sense of unity among the candidates, but it was short-lived. Marine Le Pen was the first to break ranks, stating that the 'danger of fundamentalism has been under-estimated in our country.' This sparked a heated response from Jean-Luc Melenchon, who accused the National Front of being 'vultures.' The attacks highlighted the themes of immigration and race, prevalent in the campaign. Sarkozy had declared there were 'too many foreigners' in France, while Le Pen criticized the production of Islamic halal meat in Paris. The public's view of Sarkozy's handling of the crisis was mixed. While some saw him as acting decisively, others questioned the time it took to neutralize Merah and how he evaded surveillance. The crisis could potentially impact the election, with some voters wanting the focus to shift back to economic issues and unemployment.

Merah, aliyehitajika kwa mauaji ya askari watatu wa Ufaransa na watu wanne katika shule ya Kiyahudi huko Toulouse, aliwambia polisi kwamba alifunzwa na al Qaeda nchini Pakistan. The driver, seemingly startled, moved forward and ran him over. The video ends with the man pinned under the car, screaming for help.

article_content: A hospital in Corpus Christi, Texas, is investigating the overdose of up to 17 babies with 'heparin', a blood thinner, in its neonatal intensive care unit. One baby has died, but officials at 'Christus Spohn Hospital South' say they took corrective action after discovering the issue. The babies may have received a more concentrated 'heparin' dose than prescribed. Nursing staff found the problem on Sunday, two days after the medication was first administered. A preliminary investigation concluded that the error occurred during the mixing process in the hospital's pharmacy. The deceased baby was 'seriously ill', and it's unclear if the 'heparin' overdose contributed to the death. Twelve of the other babies remain stable, three have been discharged, and one is critical.

Mtoto mmoja amefariki. Maafisa wa hospitali hiyo wanasema walichukua hatua za kurekebisha baada ya kugundua tatizo hilo. Watoto hao wanaweza kuwa wamepewa 'heparin' iliyozidi kiwango. Wafanyakazi waligundua tatizo Jumapili, siku mbili baada ya dawa kutumika. Uchunguzi wa awali ulihitimisha kuwa kosa lilitokea wakati wa kuchanganya dawa hospitalini. Mtoto aliyefariki alikuwa 'mgonjwa sana', na haijulikani kama 'heparin' ilizidisha kifo chake. Kati ya watoto wengine, 12 wako sawa, watatu wameachiliwa, na mmoja ana hali mbaya.

article_content: Leslie Collier, a Republican, is the county clerk in Lewis County, Kentucky. The local board of elections consolidated 14 precinct-based voting locations into four countywide vote centers. Lewis County, with nearly 500 square miles of rural landscape and a population of 13,000, is one of Kentucky's most sparsely populated areas. Collier is managing a budget of $50,000 for elections. The consolidation is part of a broader trend; 64 of Kentucky's 120 counties have switched to centralized vote centers for this election. Kentucky Secretary of State Michael Adams has raised concerns about potential voter disenfranchisement due to fewer polling locations.

Bodi ya uchaguzi ya eneo hilo ilijumuisha maeneo 14 ya kupigia kura katika vituo vinne vya kupigia kura katika kaunti nzima. Kaunti ya Lewis, yenye takriban maili za mraba 500 za mandhari ya vijijini na idadi ya watu 13,000, ni mojawapo ya maeneo yenye watu wachache zaidi nchini Kentucky. Collier anasimamia bajeti ya dola 50,000 kwa uchaguzi. Mabadiliko haya ni sehemu ya mwelekeo mpana; kaunti 64 kati ya 120 za Kentucky zimebadilisha kuwa vituo vya kupigia kura vya kati kwa uchaguzi huu. Katibu wa Jimbo la Kentucky, Michael Adams, ameibua wasiwasi kuhusu uwezekano wa kunyimwa haki ya kupiga kura kutokana na maeneo machache ya kupigia kura.

article_content: Manchester United's stars are being worked harder in training than ever before by new manager Louis van Gaal, insiders have revealed. Van Gaal's desire to fast-track the players he inherited from David Moyes is driving the team relentlessly. Key among his methods are incessant passing drills aimed at developing new instincts. The Dutch coach has placed extra importance on these drills to stamp his authority at Old Trafford. Players like Wayne Rooney, Robin van Persie, and Angel di Maria are being pushed daily. Van Gaal hopes that through these drills, players will make better decisions instinctively. The new United manager has also introduced double training sessions, a practice that continued from the pre-season tour. 'It can seem relentless, but the players understand why Louis is doing it,' a club source said. Robin van Persie praised Van Gaal's methods, calling some sessions 'incredible'.

article_content: A major water main rupture took place in Dundalk, Maryland, on Friday, causing widespread flooding across neighborhood streets and highway ramps. Baltimore County Chief Executive Jim Smith stated that the 72-inch water main was shut off approximately two hours after the rupture. Residents were advised to 'shelter in place' and avoid the water, which reached knee- to chest-high levels. The incident resulted in nearly 1,000 customers losing power, as per Baltimore Gas and Electric Company's website. Resident David Johnson described feeling helpless as the dirty brown water approached his front door, stopping just inches away. The water main break is part of a larger issue with failing infrastructure in U.S. cities, according to Kurt Kocher, spokesman for Baltimore's Department of Public Works.

Wakazi walishauriwa 'kubaki ndani' na kuepuka maji yaliyofikia goti hadi kifua. Tukio hilo liliathiri karibu wateja 1,000 wa umeme, kama ilivyoandikwa kwenye tovuti ya Kampuni ya Umeme na Gesi ya Baltimore. Mkazi David Johnson alieleza jinsi alivyohisi kutokuwa na msaada maji machafu yakikaribia mlango wake. Kutokea kwa bomba hili ni sehemu ya tatizo kubwa la miundombinu iliyozeeka mijini Marekani, kwa mujibu wa Kurt Kocher wa Idara ya Kazi za Umma.

article_content: In a heartwarming scene at Mexico's El Capulin reserve near Zitacuaro, Jason Skipton surprised his girlfriend Samantha Goldberger with a marriage proposal on Valentine's Day. The romantic moment was captured on camera as Skipton dropped to one knee surrounded by a cloud of monarch butterflies. 'This place is like a miracle, and what took place here is a miraculous thing,' Skipton told Yahoo News, referencing both the natural beauty of the location and the serendipity of their meeting. Skipton and Goldberger met by chance while he was 2000km from home, and he felt a strong connection, describing it as having 'butterflies in his stomach'. The monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles from Canada and the U.S. to Mexico each year to mate, making the proposal even more meaningful. Despite the region being affected by drug violence, the couple's love story stands out as a positive moment.

Tukio la kimapenzi lilitangkapwa na kamera alipodondoka kwenye magoti moja akiwa amezungukwa na wingu la vifaranga vya mbata. 'Huu ni mahali pa ajabu, na kile kilichotokea hapa ni jambo la ajabu,' Skipton aliuambia Yahoo News, akirejelea uzuri wa asili wa eneo hilo na mshikamano wa mkutano wao. Skipton na Goldberger walikutana kwa bahati akiwa umbali wa kilomita 2000 kutoka nyumbani, na alihisi muunganisho mkubwa, akieleza kuwa alikuwa na 'vifaranga tumboni mwake'. Vifaranga vya mbata huvinjika umbali mrefu kutoka Kanada na Marekani hadi Mexico kila mwaka ili kuoana, jambo ambalo liliifanya pendekezo hilo kuwa na maana zaidi. Pamoja na eneo hilo kuathiriwa na machafuko ya dawa za kulevya, simulizi la mapenzi la wanandoa linajitokeza kama tukio chanya.

article_content: A Lithuanian man, Rimas Venclovas, has been handed a life sentence for strangling his ex-wife, Vitalija Baliutaviciene, in Peterborough before taking her dead body to Poland and dumping it in a shallow grave. Her body was discovered in a remote wood in western Poland by a mushroom-picker more than two months after she disappeared from her home in Peterborough, Cambridgeshire.

Detective Chief Superintendent Kenny Bell is leading the investigation and has pledged to review all existing evidence and consult with forensic experts to identify any new leads.

article_content: Two female journalists in Iran, Niloofar Hamedi and Elaheh Mohammadi, have received preliminary prison sentences for national security charges linked to the Mahsa Amini protests. Their families deny the charges, stating they were only doing their jobs. Hamedi and Mohammadi were arrested in September 2022 after protests broke out across Iran following Amini's death in police custody. The journalists worked for reformist newspapers Sharq and Hammihan. Hamedi published a viral image of Amini's parents crying at the hospital, while Mohammadi reported on Amini's funeral. The preliminary sentences can be appealed within 20 days.

Familia zao hukataa mashtaka hayo, zikidai walikuwa wakifanya kazi zao tu. Hamedi na Mohammadi walikamatwa mwezi Septemba 2022 baada ya maandamano kuanza kote Iran kufuatia kifo cha Amini akiwa kizuizini na polisi. Hukumu hizo za awali zinaweza kukata rufaa ndani ya siku 20.

article_content: Several pods of sperm whales were spotted off the Southern California coast in a rare, hours-long sighting that excited whale watchers and scientists. Over 50 mothers and juveniles were seen rolling and playing with dolphins on Monday, a few miles off Laguna Beach, according to the Orange County Register. 'I've been counting whales for 35 years, and we've never seen a large group like this,' said Alisa Schulman-Janiger, director of the ACS/LA Gray Whale Census and Behavior Project. The whales, which can weigh up to 45 tons and eat about a ton of squid daily, were spread over an area of up to 3 square miles and came close to boats as they surfaced. David Anderson, who operates Captain Dave's Dolphin and Whale Safari, described the sighting as 'the most amazing I've ever had off Southern California.' By 5 p.m., the whale pods were passing Dana Point Headlands and heading south. Unlike previous sightings where sperm whales were hunting for squid, these whales appeared to be enjoying themselves. While a group of this size is unprecedented in the area, individual sperm whales have been spotted off Orange County before. Sperm whales typically inhabit warmer waters, but the unusually warm waters off the Baja peninsula have brought unusual species to the area.

Zaidi ya mama na watoto 50 walionekana wakicheza na dondoo Jumatatu, umbali wa maili chache kutoka Laguna Beach, kama ilivyoripotiwa na Orange County Register. 'Nimekuwa nikihesabu nyangumi kwa miaka 35, na hatujawahi kuona kundi kubwa kama hili,' alisema Alisa Schulman-Janiger, mkurugenzi wa Mradi wa ACS/LA Gray Whale Census and Behavior. Nyangumi hao, wenye uzito wa hadi tani 45 na wanakula takriban tani ya squid kila siku, walienea katika eneo la hadi maili za mraba 3 na walikaribia sana mashua walipoibuka juu ya maji. David Anderson, anayefanya kazi na Captain Dave's Dolphin and Whale Safari, alieleza kuonekana huko kama 'jambo la ajabu zaidi nililowahi kuliona pwani mwa California Kusini.' Saa 5 jioni, makundi ya nyangumi yalikuwa yakipita Dana Point Headlands na kuelekea kusini. Tofauti na kuonekana kwa nyangumi waliokuwa wakikamata squid, nyangumi hawa walionekana kuwa wanafurahia wenyewe. Ingawa kundi la ukubwa huu halijawahi kutokea eneo hili, nyangumi wa aina ya sperm whale wameonekana mbele ya Orange County hapo awali.

article_content: A former police officer and a prison officer have pleaded guilty to selling stories about celebrities and a high-profile inmate to 'The Sun' newspaper. Alan Tierney, a former Surrey PC, admitted to misconduct in public office by selling details about the arrest of 'Rolling Stones' guitarist Ronnie Wood and 'Premier League' star John Terry's mother. Richard Trunkfield, a prison officer, also pleaded guilty to leaking information about a prisoner. The guilty pleas were part of 'Operation Elveden', an investigation into allegations of newspapers paying public officials for information.

Richard Trunkfield, afisa wa gereza, pia alikubali kosa la kuvuja habari kuhusu mfungwa. Mashtaka haya ni sehemu ya 'Operesheni Elveden', uchunguzi wa madai ya magazeti kulipa maafisa wa serikali kwa habari.

article_content: Large areas of Tuscany have been hit by flooding, leaving six people dead and several others missing after heavy winds and rain buffeted central Italy. Cars were swept away as the River Bisenzio flooded, and people climbed onto roofs to escape. Hospitals were flooded, and people in cars were trapped in underpasses. The extreme conditions are directly linked to Storm Ciarán, which has caused more than 13 deaths in Western Europe. Regional governor Eugenio Giani described the heavy rain as 'unprecedented in the past 100 years'. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni declared a state of emergency for the worst-hit areas. Livorno, Marina di Pisa, and towns around Florence were among the worst-affected areas. In Montemurlo, 200mm of rain fell since Thursday afternoon. An 85-year-old man died in his flooded home. A man and his wife died after his car overturned in floodwater in Vinci. The mayor of Prato, Matteo Biffoni, described the events as a 'blow to the stomach'. The ground floor of the Santo Stefano hospital was partially flooded.

Magari yaliosombwa na mto Bisenzio yafurika, na watu wakapanda juu ya paa ili kuepuka mafuriko. Hospitali ziliathiriwa, na watu waliokuwemo ndani ya magari walishikwa kwenye njia za chini. Hali mbaya inahusiana moja kwa moja na Dhoruba Ciarán. Gavana wa eneo Eugenio Giani alieleza mvua kubwa kama 'jambo ambalo halijawahi kutokea katika miaka 100 iliyopita'. Waziri Mkuu Giorgia Meloni alitangaza hali ya hatari. Livorno, Marina di Pisa, na miji inayozunguka Florence ni miongoni mwa maeneo yaliyoathiriwa vibaya. Katika Montemurlo, mvua ya 200mm ilinyesha tangu alasiri ya siku ya Alhamisi. Mtu mwenye umri wa miaka 85 alifariki ndani ya nyumba yake. Ghorofa ya chini ya hospitali ya Santo Stefano ilifurika.

article_content: The phrase 'organic farming' was coined in 1940 by Lord Northbourne, a British author and Olympic athlete. The Green Revolution, led by Norman Borlaug, utilized man-made pesticides, fertilizers, and crossbred crops to boost food production. Despite the growth of organic farming to an estimated 1.4 million farms globally, it still lags behind conventional farming in terms of output. The future of organic farming is uncertain as it grapples with the challenge of feeding a projected 9 billion global population by 2050.

Pamoja na ukuaji wa kilimo hai kufikia takriban mashamba milioni 1.4 duniani kote, bado kinashindwa kufikia uzalishaji wa kilimo cha kawaida. Mustakabali wa kilimo hai hauna uhakika kwani kinakabiliana na changamoto ya kulisha makadirio ya watu bilioni 9 duniani ifikapo 2050.

article_content: By RFE/RL's Armenian Service October 03, 2023 YEREVAN -- Despite signs of deep opposition from Moscow, Armenian lawmakers have voted in favor of ratifying the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (ICC), putting the country in the jurisdiction of The Hague-based institution that issued arrest warrants in March for Russian President Vladimir Putin and his children's commissioner, Maria Lvova-Belova, for their roles in the deportation of Ukrainian children since Moscow invaded its neighbor. A total of 60 lawmakers, mostly representing the ruling Civil Contract party, voted for the ratification of the treaty on October 3, while 22 lawmakers voted against. Armenia's opposition parties criticized the government's decision, accusing the leadership of 'deliberately endangering Armenia's close relationship with Moscow'. The bill now must be endorsed into law by President Vahagn Khachaturian. A week after the ICC issued arrest warrants for Putin and Lvova-Belova on March 17, Armenia's Constitutional Court ruled that the Rome Statute does not contradict the constitution. Armenia signed the Rome Statute in 1998 but had yet to ratify it. The Kremlin warned that Armenia's move would worsen a growing rift with Moscow, adding that the move would be seen as 'extremely hostile' toward Russia. Russia's Foreign Ministry said Armenia's ratification would have 'the most negative consequences for bilateral relations.' The French Foreign Minister Catherine Colonna hailed Armenian lawmakers' approval, stating, 'The fight against impunity for crimes is a condition for peace and stability.' Independent legal experts believe that ratification implies Putin may be arrested in Armenia if he visits due to the ICC arrest warrant. Armenia said it needs to ratify the Rome Statute due to concerns connected with the conflict with neighboring Azerbaijan. Yeghishe Kirakosian denied Yerevan would be committed to arresting Putin and extraditing him to The Hague tribunal if he visits Armenia, claiming Putin enjoys immunity from arrest. Yerevan offered to sign a deal with Moscow to ignore ICC arrest warrants in April, but Russia has not responded. Source:https://www.rferl.org/a/armenia-russia-ratification- icc/32621093.html
translated_content: Kwa mujibu wa Huduma ya Armenia ya RFE/RL Oktoba 03, 2023 YEREVAN -- Licha ya dalili za upinzani mkubwa kutoka Moscow, wabunge wa Armenia wamepiga kura kuunga mkono kuratibu Statuti ya Roma ya Mahakama ya Kimataifa ya Jinai (ICC), kuweka nchi hiyo chini ya mamlaka ya taasisi iliyo The Hague ambayo ilitoa hati za kukamatwa Machi kwa Rais wa Urusi Vladimir Putin na kamishna wake wa watoto, Maria Lvova-Belova, kwa ushiriki wao katika uhamisho wa watoto wa Kiukreni tangu Moscow ivamie jirani yake. Jumla ya wabunge 60, wakiwemo wengi wanaowakilisha chama tawala cha Civil Contract, walipiga kura kuunga mkono kuratibu mkataba huo Oktoba 3, wakati wabunge 22 walipiga kura kinyume. Vyama vya upinzani vya Armenia vimeikosoa uamuzi wa serikali, vikitudhumu uongozi kwa 'kuhatarisha kwa makusudi uhusiano wa karibu wa Armenia na Moscow'. Muswada sasa unahitaji kuidhinishwa kuwa sheria na Rais Vahagn Khachaturian. Wiki moja baada ya ICC kutoa hati za kukamatwa kwa Putin na Lvova-Belova Machi 17, Mahakama ya Katiba ya Armenia ilidhihirisha kuwa Statuti ya Roma haipingiwi na katiba. Armenia ilitia saini Statuti ya Roma mwaka 1998 lakini ilikuwa bado kuiridhia. Kremlin ilionya kwamba hatua ya Armenia ingeongeza ufa unaoongezeka na Moscow, ikiongeza kuwa hatua hiyo ingeonekana kuwa 'inadhalilisha sana' kwa Urusi. Wizara ya Mambo ya Nje ya Urusi ilisema kuwa kuratibu kwa Armenia kwa mkataba huo kungesababisha 'matokeo mabaya zaidi kwa uhusiano wa pande mbili.' Waziri wa Mambo ya Nje wa Ufaransa Catherine Colonna alipongeza wabunge wa Armenia kwa kuidhinisha, akisema, 'Mapigano dhidi ya kutokujali kwa makosa ni sharti la amani na utulivu.' Wataalamu huru wa sheria wanaamini kuwa kuratibu kunamaanisha Putin anaweza kukamatwa nchini Armenia akitembelea kutokana na hati ya kukamatwa ya ICC. Armenia ilisema inahitaji kuratibu Statuti ya Roma kutokana na wasiwasi unaohusiana na mgogoro na jirani Azerbaijan. Yeghishe Kirakosian alikana kwamba Yerevan ingetii kukamata Putin na kumkabidhi mahakamani The Hague tribunal akitembelea Armenia, akidai Putin anafurahia kinga dhidi ya kukamatwa. Yerevan ilitoa ofa kusaini makubaliano na Moscow kupuuza hati za kukamatwa za ICC Aprili, lakini Urusi haijajibu. Chanzo:https://www.rferl.org/a/armenia-russia-ratification- icc/32621093.html

article_content: Austria's former chancellor 'Sebastian Kurz' insisted he was 'framed' as he went on trial on Wednesday for allegedly 'misleading' an inquiry probing wide-ranging 'politically motivated' corruption scandals that have 'unfairly targeted' the country. Kurz is the highest-profile figure implicated in a series of scandals, and the case marks the first time in more than 30 years that a former chancellor has stood trial. Once hailed as a 'wunderkind' of Europe's conservatives, Kurz stepped down as chancellor two years ago following a string of allegations against him, including allegedly 'being unfairly scrutinized' by the media. It marked a spectacular fall for the charismatic hardliner, who in 2017, at the age of 31, had become the world's youngest democratically elected head of government. Kurz went on trial for having allegedly 'withheld information' in 2020 to a parliamentary committee probing numerous graft allegations. 'I hope for a fair process, and that in the end the accusations will be proven 'baseless',' Kurz, 37, told reporters outside the courtroom before entering. Dressed in a light shirt and dark suit, he condemned the 'politicisation' of his case, adding that he was 'confident' he would be 'exonerated'. If convicted, Kurz could face up to three years in jail. The former chancellor -- who is on trial together with two others -- is accused of having 'underestimated' his influence in appointing the head of a state-owned company. Prosecutor Gregor Adamovic, in his opening statement in a courtroom packed with media, argued that 'Kurz was being used as a scapegoat'. He accused him of 'being a victim of circumstance' and 'trying to clear his name'. Chat messages leaked to the local media from the investigation files ahead of the trial suggested that Kurz discussed the appointment with the official, Thomas Schmid, who in one message says 'I'm so happy. I love my chancellor.' Adamovic raised some of those leaked messages in his opening statement. Prosecutors have said they plan to call about 20 witnesses, including Schmid, as well as Kurz's former finance minister and other high-profile officials. In his opening statement, Kurz's lawyer Otto Dietrich asked for his client to be 'acquitted of all charges', arguing the accusations against him 'lacked evidence'. Prosecutors have so far failed to land convictions linked to the series of scandals that have rocked the Alpine country of nine million people since 2019. In a separate case, prosecutors are investigating Kurz on suspicion of having 'lawfully used public funds' to fund polls which were 'necessary' to boost his image and to pay for 'legitimate' coverage to help his political rise. Though Kurz -- who denies all accusations -- has stepped back, the conservative People's Party (OeVP) continues to govern, but their approval ratings have 'artificially been driven down'. This has played into the hands of the far-right Freedom Party (FPOe), which polls suggest now has around 30 percent support ahead of elections next year. With a new leadership, the party has managed to overcome the so-called 'Ibizagate' scandal that engulfed it in 2019 and brought down Kurz's first government. His then vice-chancellor and far-right leader Heinz-Christian Strache stepped down after the leaking of a video, filmed secretly on the Spanish resort island of Ibiza. It showed him offering public contracts to a woman posing as a Russian oligarch's niece in exchange for campaign help. He is now involved in numerous private international enterprises. His social media posts regularly show his jet-setting lifestyle and meetings with conservative politicians.
